newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani caretaker government plan to expand privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani caretaker government plan to expand privatisation.

text.p: Pakistan's caretaker government plans to expand and speed up the privatisation of state enterprises following the sacking of prime minister Benazir Bhutto earlier this month, a top official said on Sunday.

Salman Shah, chairman of the state Privatisation Commission, told Reuters that caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid's government would speed up the process and expand it to cover the state airline, airports, railways and shipping.
"We would expedite the ongoing privatisation, which means that all the hurdles and bottlenecks have to be removed...and expand the process in all the sectors of the economy," he said.

Shah said a bottleneck in privatising banking and other financial instititutions was created by their huge bad debts, estimated to be between 80 billion ($1.99 billion) and 100 billion rupees ($2.49 billion).
He said a trust corporation was being set up to assume the bad debts to improve the financial health of these institutions and thus attract buyer interest and better prices for them.
Pakistan's earlier attempt to sell a 26 percent stake and transfer of management control in the state-run United Bank Ltd (UBL) failed.

In February, Bhutto's government approved the sale of UBL to the sole bidder, the Saudi Basharahil Group, which was to have managed the bank. The deal fell through when the group failed to make agreed cash payments, the Privatisation Commission said.

In April, the State (central) Bank of Pakistan took over UBL, saying it was losing about 700 million rupees ($20 million) a year due to misappropriation and widespread abuses, including payments to about 3,000 "ghost workers".

Shah said the government was also looking at the privatisation of the national carrier Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) and some airports to increase their efficiency and raise much-needed money for national debt repayment.
He said a partial privatisation and modernisation of Pakistan Railways was also on the cards.
"We would like to have investment from foreign operators by selling shares of these and some other public enterprises," he said.

The government also plans to issue global depositary receipts (GDRs) for some of the state enterprises that may include Pakistan State Oil, power stations, oil refineries and the State Life Insurance Corporation, Shah said.
"We are looking at doing some GDRs for state enterprises so that we can establish ourselves as a regular players in the international market," he added.
Shah said the government had a very large portfolio in the public sector and issuing GDRs could ease some of the national debt burden.

Pakistan's plans to sell a 26 percent stake and transfer the management of the Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd (PTCL) had been delayed since December 1995, but Shah said it had not been shelved or put off.

"The PTCL is a very large transaction even by international standards," he said. "There are a few concerns of international buyers in regulatory and management areas of the PTCL and the government would first like to remove those."
Shah said the privatisation of the PTCL would go ahead but not before the government addressed the concerns of buyers and had a large pool of strategic investors in place.
"I am not going to throw away the PTCL," he said.
